text.en: But thou, want not! ask not! Find full reward of doing right in right! Let right deeds be thy motive, not the fruit which comes from them.
text.hi:
कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन। मा कर्मफलहेतुर्भूर्मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि॥

(अर्थ: तुम्हारा अधिकार केवल कर्म करने में है, उसके फल में कभी नहीं। फल की इच्छा से कर्म मत करो, और कर्म न करने में भी आसक्ति मत रखो।)
text.sa: कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन । मा कर्मफलहेतुर्भूर्मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि ॥

text.en: The Lord is my shepherd; I shall not want.
Therefore remember Me, I will remember you. Give thanks to Me, and reject not Me.
text.ar: فَاذْكُرُونِي أَذْكُرْكُمْ وَاشْكُرُوا لِي وَلَا تَكْفُرُونِ

source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text.en: For hatred does not cease by hatred at any time: hatred ceases by love, this is an old rule.

source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

text.en: There is but one God whose name is true, the Creator, devoid of fear and enmity, immortal, unborn, self-existent by the favour of the Guru.
text.pa: ੴ ਸਤਿ ਨਾਮੁ ਕਰਤਾ ਪੁਰਖੁ ਨਿਰਭਉ ਨਿਰਵੈਰੁ ਅਕਾਲ ਮੂਰਤਿ ਅਜੂਨੀ ਸੈਭੰ ਗੁਰ ਪ੍ਰਸਾਦਿ ॥

source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text.en: Let each man raise the Self by Soul, not trample down his Self, since Soul that is Self's friend may grow Self's foe.
text.hi:
उद्धरेदात्मनात्मानं नात्मानमवसादयेत्। आत्मैव ह्यात्मनो बन्धुरात्मैव रिपुरात्मनः॥

(अर्थ: मनुष्य को अपने द्वारा अपना उद्धार करना चाहिए, अपना पतन नहीं। आत्मा ही अपनी मित्र है और आत्मा ही अपनी शत्रु है।)
text.sa: उद्धरेदात्मनाऽऽत्मानं नात्मानमवसादयेत् । आत्मैव ह्यात्मनो बन्धुरात्मैव रिपुरात्मनः ॥

text.en: For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life.
O ye who believe! Seek help in steadfastness and prayer. Lo! Allah is with the steadfast.

source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text.en: Not the perversities of others, not their sins of commission or omission, but his own misdeeds and negligences should a sage take notice of.
text.pi: Na paresaṃ vilomāni, na paresaṃ katākataṃ; attanova avekkheyya, katāni akatāni ca.

source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

text.en: How shall man become true before God? How shall the veil of falsehood be rent? By walking, O Nanak, according to the will of the Commander as preordained.
text.pa: ਕਿਵ ਸਚਿਆਰਾ ਹੋਈਐ ਕਿਵ ਕੂੜੈ ਤੁਟੈ ਪਾਲਿ ॥ ਹੁਕਮਿ ਰਜਾਈ ਚਲਣਾ ਨਾਨਕ ਲਿਖਿਆ ਨਾਲਿ ॥

source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text.en: But to those blessed ones who worship Me, turning not otherwhere, with minds set fast, I bring assurance of full bliss beyond.
For I know the thoughts that I think toward you, saith the Lord, thoughts of peace, and not of evil, to give you an expected end.
Allah tasketh not a soul beyond its scope.
text.ar: لَا يُكَلِّفُ اللَّهُ نَفْسًا إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا

source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text.en: Rouse thyself! do not be idle! Follow the law of virtue! The virtuous rests in bliss in this world and in the next.

source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

text.en: Nanak, sing His praises who is the Treasury of excellences. Sing and hear and put His love into your hearts. Thus shall your sorrows be removed, and you shall be absorbed in Him who is the abode of happiness.

source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text.en: When Righteousness declines, O Bharata! when Wickedness is strong, I rise, from age to age, and take visible shape, and move a man with men, succouring the good, thrusting the evil back, and setting Virtue on her seat again.
text.sa: यदा यदा हि धर्मस्य ग्लानिर्भवति भारत । अभ्युत्थानमधर्मस्य तदात्मानं सृजाम्यहम् ॥

text.en: I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me.
Say: O My slaves who have been prodigal to their own hurt! Despair not of the mercy of Allah, Who forgiveth all sins. Lo! He is the Forgiving, the Merciful.

source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text.en: Not to commit any sin, to do good, and to purify one's mind, that is the teaching of (all) the Awakened.
text.pi: Sabbapāpassa akaraṇaṃ, kusalassa upasampadā; sacittapariyodapanaṃ — etaṃ buddhāna sāsanaṃ.

source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

text.en: Nanak, the saints are ever happy. By hearing the Name sorrow and sin are no more.

source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text.en: For wheresoe'er is wondrous work, and majesty, and might, from Me hath all proceeded. Receive thou this aright!
Trust in the Lord with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding.
Lo! with hardship goeth ease

source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text.en: Health is the greatest of gifts, contentedness the best riches; trust is the best of relationships, Nirvana the highest happiness.

source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

text.en: Nanak, God bestoweth gifts on whom He looketh with favour and mercy.

source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text.en: Who hateth nought of all which lives, living himself benign, compassionate, from arrogance exempt, exempt from love of self, unchangeable by good or ill; patient, contented, firm in faith, mastering himself, true to his word, seeking Me, heart and soul; vowed unto Me, that man I love!
Fear thou not; for I am with thee: be not dismayed; for I am thy God: I will strengthen thee; yea, I will help thee; yea, I will uphold thee with the right hand of my righteousness.
Who have believed and whose hearts have rest in the remembrance of Allah. Verily in the remembrance of Allah do hearts find rest!

source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text.en: Let a man overcome anger by love, let him overcome evil by good; let him overcome the greedy by liberality, the liar by truth!
text.pi: Akkodhena jine kodhaṃ, asādhuṃ sādhunā jine; jine kadariyaṃ dānena, saccenālikavādinaṃ.

source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

ref: Asa ki War, Pauri I (Guru Nanak)

text.en: O Creator, Thou art the Giver; being pleased Thou bestowest and practisest kindness.

source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text.en: And whoso thus discerneth Me in all, and all in Me, I never let him go; nor looseneth he hold upon Me; but, dwell he where he may, whate'er his life, in Me he dwells and lives, because he knows and worships Me, Who dwell in all which lives, and cleaves to Me in all.
Have not I commanded thee? Be strong and of a good courage; be not afraid, neither be thou dismayed: for the Lord thy God is with thee whithersoever thou goest.
And whosoever putteth his trust in Allah, He will suffice him.

source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text.en: Speak the truth, do not yield to anger; give, if thou art asked for little; by these three steps thou wilt go near the gods.

source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

ref: Guru Nanak's hymn to the leper (Dhanasari), Life of Guru Nanak

text.en: Even if he be drowning in sin, God will still take care of him. Nanak, the True One is beneficent to all.

source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text.en: Wake! Be thyself! Arise, Scourge of thy Foes!
God is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble.
Thee (alone) we worship; Thee (alone) we ask for help.

source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text.en: All that we are is the result of what we have thought: it is founded on our thoughts, it is made up of our thoughts. If a man speaks or acts with a pure thought, happiness follows him, like a shadow that never leaves him.

source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

text.en: By His order souls are infused into them; by His order greatness is obtained.

source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text.en: Nor I, nor thou, nor any one of these, Ever was not, nor ever will not be, For ever and for ever afterwards.
He that dwelleth in the secret place of the most High shall abide under the shadow of the Almighty.
Show us the straight path

source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text.en: "He abused me, he beat me, he defeated me, he robbed me,"--in those who do not harbour such thoughts hatred will cease.

source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

text.en: The Giver giveth; the receiver groweth weary of receiving. In every age man subsisteth by His bounty.

source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text.en: The soul which is not moved, The soul that with a strong and constant calm Takes sorrow and takes joy indifferently, Lives in the life undying!
I will lift up mine eyes unto the hills, from whence cometh my help. My help cometh from the LORD, which made heaven and earth.

And when My servants question thee concerning Me, then surely I am nigh. I answer the prayer of the suppliant when he crieth unto Me. So let them hear My call and let them trust in Me, in order that they may be led aright.

source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text.en: As rain does not break through a well-thatched house, passion will not break through a well-reflecting mind.

source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

text.en: In describing Him there would never be an end. Millions of men give millions upon millions of descriptions of Him, but they fail to describe Him.

source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text.en: Indestructible, Learn thou! the Life is, spreading life through all; It cannot anywhere, by any means, Be anywise diminished, stayed, or changed.
The LORD is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear? the LORD is the strength of my life; of whom shall I be afraid?
Spend your wealth for the cause of Allah, and be not cast by your own hands to ruin; and do good. Lo! Allah loveth the beneficent.

source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text.en: These wise people, meditative, steady, always possessed of strong powers, attain to Nirvana, the highest happiness.

source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

text.en: Who can sing Him, who is all-seeing and omnipresent?

source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text.en: Nay, but as when one layeth His worn-out robes away, And taking new ones, sayeth, 'These will I wear to-day!' So putteth by the spirit Lightly its garb of flesh, And passeth to inherit A residence afresh.
O taste and see that the LORD is good: blessed is the man that trusteth in him.
Truly Allah loveth those who turn unto Him, and loveth those who have a care for cleanness.

source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text.en: By rousing himself, by earnestness, by restraint and control, the wise man may make for himself an island which no flood can overwhelm.

source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

text.en: True is the Lord, true is His name; it is uttered with endless love.

source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text.en: Here shall no end be hindered, no hope marred, No loss be feared: faith--yea, a little faith-- Shall save thee from the anguish of thy dread.
Delight thyself also in the LORD; and he shall give thee the desires of thine heart.

The likeness of those who spend their wealth in Allah's way is as the likeness of a grain which groweth seven ears, in every ear a hundred grains. Allah giveth increase manifold to whom He will. Allah is All-Embracing, All-Knowing.

source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text.en: It is good to tame the mind, which is difficult to hold in and flighty, rushing wherever it listeth; a tamed mind brings happiness.

source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

text.en: At the ambrosial hour of morning meditate on the true Name and God's greatness.

source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text.en: And like the ocean, day by day receiving Floods from all lands, which never overflows Its boundary-line not leaping, and not leaving, Fed by the rivers, but unswelled by those;-- So is the perfect one! to his soul's ocean The world of sense pours streams of witchery; They leave him as they find, without commotion, Taking their tribute, but remaining sea.
Cast thy burden upon the LORD, and he shall sustain thee: he shall never suffer the righteous to be moved.
Ye are the best community that hath been raised up for mankind. Ye enjoin right conduct and forbid indecency; and ye believe in Allah.

source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text.en: Let the wise man guard his thoughts, for they are difficult to perceive, very artful, and they rush wherever they list: thoughts well guarded bring happiness.

source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

text.en: The Kind One will give us a robe of honour, and by His favour we shall reach the gate of salvation.

source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text.en: Work is more excellent than idleness; The body's life proceeds not, lacking work.
For the LORD is good; his mercy is everlasting; and his truth endureth to all generations.

And vie one with another for forgiveness from your Lord, and for a paradise as wide as are the heavens and the earth, prepared for those who ward off (evil); Those who spend (of that which Allah hath given them) in ease and in adversity, those who control their wrath and are forgiving toward mankind; Allah loveth the good

source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text.en: Not a mother, not a father will do so much, nor any other relative; a well-directed mind will do us greater service.

source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

text.en: That there is but one Bestower on all living beings; may I not forget Him!

source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text.en: Therefore, thy task prescribed With spirit unattached gladly perform, Since in performance of plain duty man Mounts to his highest bliss.
The LORD is merciful and gracious, slow to anger, and plenteous in mercy.
Faint not nor grieve, for ye will overcome them if ye are (indeed) believers.
text.ar: وَلَا تَهِنُوا وَلَا تَحْزَنُوا وَأَنْتُمُ الْأَعْلَوْنَ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ

source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text.en: As the bee collects nectar and departs without injuring the flower, or its colour or scent, so let a sage dwell in his village.

source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

text.en: Precious stones, jewels, and gems shall be treasured up in thy heart if thou hearken to even one word of the Guru.

source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text.en: What the wise choose The unwise people take; what best men do The multitude will follow.
This is the day which the LORD hath made; we will rejoice and be glad in it.
If Allah is your helper none can overcome you, and if He withdraw His help from you, who is there who can help you after Him ? In Allah let believers put their trust.

source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text.en: The scent of flowers does not travel against the wind, nor (that of) sandal-wood, or of Tagara and Mallika flowers; but the odour of good people travels even against the wind; a good man pervades every place.

source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

text.en: If I please Him, that is my place of pilgrimage to bathe in; if I please Him not, what ablutions shall I make?

source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text.en: Many there be who come! from fear set free, From anger, from desire; keeping their hearts Fixed upon me--my Faithful--purified By sacred flame of Knowledge. Such as these Mix with my being.
Thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path.
O ye who believe! Endure, outdo all others in endurance, be ready, and observe your duty to Allah, in order that ye may succeed.

source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text.en: If an intelligent man be associated for one minute only with a wise man, he will soon perceive the truth, as the tongue perceives the taste of soup.

source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

text.en: Nanak, God may bestow virtue on those who are devoid of it, as well as on those who already possess it; But no such person is seen as can bestow virtue upon Him.

source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text.en: All's then God! The sacrifice is Brahm, the ghee and grain Are Brahm, the fire is Brahm, the flesh it eats Is Brahm, and unto Brahm attaineth he Who, in such office, meditates on Brahm.
I will praise thee; for I am fearfully and wonderfully made: marvellous are thy works; and that my soul knoweth right well.
Allah would make the burden light for you, for man was created weak.

source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text.en: No, that deed is well done of which a man does not repent, and the reward of which he receives gladly and cheerfully.

source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

text.en: By hearing the Name even the low become highly lauded.

source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text.en: The sacrifice Which Knowledge pays is better than great gifts Offered by wealth, since gifts' worth--O my Prince! Lies in the mind which gives, the will that serves: And these are gained by reverence, by strong search, By humble heed of those who see the Truth And teach it.
He healeth the broken in heart, and bindeth up their wounds.
Yet whoso doeth evil or wrongeth his own soul, then seeketh pardon of Allah, will find Allah Forgiving, Merciful.

source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text.en: He who drinks in the law lives happily with a serene mind: the sage rejoices always in the law, as preached by the elect (Ariyas).

source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

text.en: By hearing the Name truth, contentment, and divine knowledge are obtained.

source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text.en: Believing, he receives it when the soul Masters itself, and cleaves to Truth, and comes-- Possessing knowledge--to the higher peace, The uttermost repose.
Thou wilt shew me the path of life: in thy presence is fulness of joy; at thy right hand there are pleasures for evermore.
Lo! the mercy of Allah is nigh unto the good.

source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text.en: As a solid rock is not shaken by the wind, wise people falter not amidst blame and praise.

source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

text.en: By hearing the Name the mind is composed and fixed on God.

source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text.en: He that acts in thought of Brahm, Detaching end from act, with act content, The world of sense can no more stain his soul Than waters mar th' enamelled lotus-leaf.
Let the words of my mouth, and the meditation of my heart, be acceptable in thy sight, O LORD, my strength, and my redeemer.
Say: Naught befalleth us save that which Allah hath decreed for us. He is our Protecting Friend. In Allah let believers put their trust!

source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text.en: His thought is quiet, quiet are his word and deed, when he has obtained freedom by true knowledge, when he has thus become a quiet man.

source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

text.en: Hearing the Name is equal to bathing at the sixty-eight places of pilgrimage.

source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text.en: The sage whose soul Holds off from outer contacts, in himself Finds bliss; to Brahma joined by piety, His spirit tastes eternal peace.
In all thy ways acknowledge him, and he shall direct thy paths.
Go, O my sons, and ascertain concerning Joseph and his brother, and despair not of the Spirit of Allah.

source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text.en: Forests are delightful; where the world finds no delight, there the passionless will find delight, for they look not for pleasures.

source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

text.en: By hearing the Name, the depth of the sea of virtue is sounded.

source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text.en: Yea! for he knows Me Who am He that heeds The sacrifice and worship, God revealed; And He who heeds not, being Lord of Worlds, Lover of all that lives, God unrevealed, Wherein who will shall find surety and shield!
Commit thy works unto the LORD, and thy thoughts shall be established.
And whatever of comfort ye enjoy, it is from Allah. Then, when misfortune reacheth you, unto Him ye cry for help.

source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text.en: If one man conquer in battle a thousand times thousand men, and if another conquer himself, he is the greatest of conquerors.

source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

text.en: By hearing the Name a blind man findeth his way. By hearing the Name the unfathomable becometh fathomable.

source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text.en: Therefore, who doeth work rightful to do, Not seeking gain from work, that man, O Prince! Is Sanyasi and Yogi--both in one And he is neither who lights not the flame Of sacrifice, nor setteth hand to task.
The name of the LORD is a strong tower: the righteous runneth into it, and is safe.
Whosoever doeth right, whether male or female, and is a believer, him verily we shall quicken with good life, and We shall pay them a recompense in proportion to the best of what they used to do.

source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text.en: He who always greets and constantly reveres the aged, four things will increase to him, viz. life, beauty, happiness, power.

source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

text.en: So pure is His name—Whoever obeyeth God knoweth the pleasure of it in his own heart.

source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text.en: Let each man raise The Self by Soul, not trample down his Self, Since Soul that is Self's friend may grow Self's foe.
Thou wilt keep him in perfect peace, whose mind is stayed on thee: because he trusteth in thee.
And say: My Lord! Cause me to come in with a firm incoming and to go out with a firm outgoing. And give me from Thy presence a sustaining Power.

source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text.en: If a man does what is good, let him do it again; let him delight in it: happiness is the outcome of good.

source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

text.en: There is no limit to His mercy, and to His gifts there is no limit.

source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text.en: That Yojin, so devoted, so controlled, Comes to the peace beyond,--My peace, the peace Of high Nirvana!
He giveth power to the faint; and to them that have no might he increaseth strength.
And say: Truth hath come and falsehood hath vanished away. Lo! falsehood is ever bound to vanish.

source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text.en: Let no man think lightly of good, saying in his heart, It will not come nigh unto me. Even by the falling of water-drops a water-pot is filled; the wise man becomes full of good, even if he gather it little by little.

source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

text.en: By obeying Him man attaineth the gate of salvation.

source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text.en: Steadfast a lamp burns sheltered from the wind; Such is the likeness of the Yogi's mind Shut from sense-storms and burning bright to Heaven.
But they that wait upon the LORD shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles; they shall run, and not be weary; and they shall walk, and not faint.
And lo! verily I am Forgiving toward him who repenteth and believeth and doeth good, and afterward walketh aright.

source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text.en: If, like a shattered metal plate (gong), thou utter not, then thou hast reached Nirvana; contention is not known to thee.

source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

text.en: What power and beautiful form are Thine, O God! Who hath power to know how great Thy gifts are?

source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text.en: I will declare to thee that utmost lore, Whole and particular, which, when thou knowest, Leaveth no more to know here in this world.

When thou passest through the waters, I will be with thee; and through the rivers, they shall not overflow thee: when thou walkest through the fire, thou shalt not be burned; neither shall the flame kindle upon thee.
We said: O fire, be coolness and peace for Abraham

source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text.en: He who, though dressed in fine apparel, exercises tranquillity, is quiet, subdued, restrained, chaste, and has ceased to find fault with all other beings, he indeed is a Brahmana, an ascetic (sramana), a friar (bhikshu).

source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

text.en: Whatever pleaseth Thee is good. Thou, O Formless One, art ever secure.

source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text.en: I am the fresh taste of the water; I The silver of the moon, the gold o' the sun, The word of worship in the Veds, the thrill That passeth in the ether, and the strength Of man's shed seed.
Call unto me, and I will answer thee, and shew thee great and mighty things, which thou knowest not.
Successful indeed are the believers Who are humble in their prayers

source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text.en: If a man hold himself dear, let him watch himself carefully; during one at least out of the three watches a wise man should be watchful.

source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

text.en: So powerless am I, that I cannot even once be a sacrifice unto Thee.

source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text.en: All four are good, and seek me; but mine own, The true of heart, the faithful--stayed on me, Taking me as their utmost blessedness, They are not 'mine,' but I--even I myself! At end of many births to Me they come!
It is of the LORD’S mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not. They are new every morning: great is thy faithfulness.

The (faithful) slaves of the Beneficent are they who walk upon the earth modestly, and when the foolish ones address them answer: Peace; And who spend the night before their Lord, prostrate and standing

source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text.en: Self is the lord of self, who else could be the lord? With self well subdued, a man finds a lord such as few can find.

source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

text.en: Numberless thy worshippers, and numberless Thy lovers.

source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text.en: Have Me, then, in thy heart always!
He hath shewed thee, O man, what is good; and what doth the LORD require of thee, but to do justly, and to love mercy, and to walk humbly with thy God?

Save him who repenteth and believeth and doth righteous work; as for such, Allah will change their evil deeds to good deeds. Allah is ever Forgiving, Merciful. And whosoever repenteth and doeth good, he verily repenteth toward Allah with true repentance

source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text.en: He who formerly was reckless and afterwards became sober, brightens up this world, like the moon when freed from clouds.

source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

text.en: Numberless Thy silent worshippers who lovingly fix their thoughts upon Thee.

source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text.en: But--higher, deeper, innermost--abides Another Life, not like the life of sense, Escaping sight, unchanging.
The LORD is good, a strong hold in the day of trouble; and he knoweth them that trust in him.
And when I sicken, then He healeth me, And Who causeth me to die, then giveth me life (again)

source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text.en: The uncharitable do not go to the world of the gods; fools only do not praise liberality; a wise man rejoices in liberality, and through it becomes blessed in the other world.

source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

text.en: Numberless Thy names, and numberless Thy places.

source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text.en: Richer than holy fruit on Vedas growing, Greater than gifts, better than prayer or fast, Such wisdom is! The Yogi, this way knowing, Comes to the Utmost Perfect Peace at last.
The LORD thy God in the midst of thee is mighty; he will save, he will rejoice over thee with joy; he will rest in his love, he will joy over thee with singing.
Who persevere, and put their trust in their Lord!

source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text.en: Even the gods envy those who are awakened and not forgetful, who are given to meditation, who are wise, and who delight in the repose of retirement (from the world).

source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

text.en: Numberless they who repeat Thy name with all the strength of their intellects.

source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text.en: By Me the whole vast Universe of things Is spread abroad;--by Me, the Unmanifest! In Me are all existences contained; Not I in them!
Be strong and of a good courage, fear not, nor be afraid of them: for the LORD thy God, he it is that doth go with thee; he will not fail thee, nor forsake thee.
As for those who strive in Us, We surely guide them to Our paths, and lo! Allah is with the good.

source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text.en: Happy is the arising of the awakened, happy is the teaching of the True Law, happy is peace in the church, happy is the devotion of those who are at peace.

source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

text.en: As great Thy creation, O God, so great is Thy fame. There is no place without Thy name.

source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text.en: See! as the shoreless airs Move in the measureless space, but are not space, [And space were space without the moving airs]; So all things are in Me, but are not I.
Blessed are the peacemakers: for they shall be called the children of God.

And of His signs is this: He created for you helpmeets from yourselves that ye might find rest in them, and He ordained between you love and mercy. Lo! herein indeed are portents for folk who reflect.

source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text.en: Let us live happily then, not hating those who hate us! among men who hate us let us dwell free from hatred!

source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

text.en: So when the mind is defiled by sin, It is cleansed by the love of the Name.

source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text.en: Whoso shall offer Me in faith and love A leaf, a flower, a fruit, water poured forth, That offering I accept, lovingly made With pious will.
But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you.
He it is Who blesseth you, and His angels (bless you), that He may bring you forth from darkness unto light; and He is ever Merciful to the believers.

source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text.en: Let us live happily then, though we call nothing our own! We shall be like the bright gods, feeding on happiness!

source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

text.en: But he who heareth and obeyeth and loveth God in his heart, Shall wash off his impurity in the place of pilgrimage within him.

source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text.en: They are in Me, and I in them!
Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.
That which Allah openeth unto mankind of mercy none can withhold it; and that which He withholdeth none can release thereafter. He is the Mighty, the Wise.

source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text.en: Victory breeds hatred, for the conquered is unhappy. He who has given up both victory and defeat, he, the contented, is happy.

source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

text.en: All virtues are Thine, O Lord; none are mine.

source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text.en: And, all for love of them, within their darkened souls I dwell, And, with bright rays of wisdom's lamp, their ignorance dispel.
But Jesus beheld them, and said unto them, With men this is impossible; but with God all things are possible.
The word from a Merciful Lord (for them) is: Peace!

source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text.en: He who possesses virtue and intelligence, who is just, speaks the truth, and does what is his own business, him the world will hold dear.

source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

text.en: Great is the Lord, great is His name; what He doeth cometh to pass.

source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text.en: For wheresoe'er is wondrous work, and majesty, and might, From Me hath all proceeded. Receive thou this aright!
Therefore I say unto you, What things soever ye desire, when ye pray, believe that ye receive them, and ye shall havethem.
For those who do good in this world there is good, and Allah's earth is spacious. Verily the steadfast will be paid their wages without stint.

source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text.en: Kinsmen, friends, and lovers salute a man who has been long away, and returns safe from afar.

source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

text.en: Hail! Hail to Him, The primal, the pure, without beginning, the indestructible, the same in every age!

source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text.en: Of poets Usana, of saints Vyasa, sage divine; The policy of conquerors, the potency of kings, The great unbroken silence in learning's secret things; The lore of all the learned, the seed of all which springs.
For with God nothing shall be impossible.
Lo! the promise of Allah is true. And ask forgiveness of thy sin, and hymn the praise of thy Lord at fall of night and in the early hours.

source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text.en: He who holds back rising anger like a rolling chariot, him I call a real driver; other people are but holding the reins.

source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

ref: Asa ki War, Slok II (Guru Nanak)

text.en: True Thy praises, true Thy eulogies; True Thy might, O true King.

source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text.en: If there should rise Suddenly within the skies Sunburst of a thousand suns Flooding earth with beams undeemed-of, Then might be that Holy One's Majesty and radiance dreamed of!
Then spake Jesus again unto them, saying, I am the light of the world: he that followeth me shall not walk in darkness, but shall have the light of life.
And your Lord hath said: Pray unto Me and I will hear your prayer.

source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text.en: Those who are ever watchful, who study day and night, and who strive after Nirvana, their passions will come to an end.

source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

ref: Asa ki War, Slok II (Guru Nanak)

text.en: Nanak, true are they who meditate on the True One.

source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text.en: Who doeth all for Me; who findeth Me In all; adoreth always; loveth all Which I have made, and Me, for Love's sole end That man, Arjuna! unto Me doth wend.
Peace I leave with you, my peace I give unto you: not as the world giveth, give I unto you. Let not your heart be troubled, neither let it be afraid.
Allah is gracious unto His slaves. He provideth for whom He will. And He is the Strong, the Mighty.

source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text.en: Let a wise man blow off the impurities of his self, as a smith blows off the impurities of silver one by one, little by little, and from time to time.

source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

ref: Asa ki War, Slok III (Guru Nanak)

text.en: Wonderful Thy word, wonderful Thy knowledge; Wonderful Thy creatures, wonderful their species.

source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text.en: Cling thou to Me! Clasp Me with heart and mind! so shalt thou dwell Surely with Me on high.
These things I have spoken unto you, that in me ye might have peace. In the world ye shall have tribulation: but be of good cheer; I have overcome the world.
Now whatever ye have been given is but a passing comfort for the life of the world, and that which Allah hath is better and more lasting for those who believe and put their trust in their Lord

source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text.en: He in whom that feeling is destroyed, and taken out with the very root, finds rest by day and by night.

source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

ref: Asa ki War, Slok III (Guru Nanak)

text.en: Wonderful to behold Thee present. Beholding these wonderful things I remain wondering.

source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text.en: And, if thou canst not worship steadfastly, Work for Me, toil in works pleasing to Me! For he that laboureth right for love of Me Shall finally attain!
And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose.

Lo! those who say: Our Lord is Allah, and thereafter walk aright, there shall no fear come upon them neither shall they grieve. Such are rightful owners of the Garden, immortal therein, as a reward for what they used to do.

source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text.en: A man is not learned because he talks much; he who is patient, free from hatred and fear, he is called learned.

source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

text.en: Everything existeth by Thy power; Thou art the omnipotent Creator; Thy name is the holiest of the holy. Saith Nanak, Thou beholdest and pervadest all things subject to Thy command: Thou art altogether unrivalled.

source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text.en: bring Me thy failure! find Refuge in Me!

We verily created man and We know what his soul whispereth to him, and We are nearer to him than his jugular vein.

source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text.en: A man is not an elect (Ariya) because he injures living creatures; because he has pity on all living creatures, therefore is a man called Ariya.

source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

ref: Asa ki War, Pauri IV (Guru Nanak)

text.en: There is no benefactor so great as the true Guru; hear this, all ye people.

source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text.en: But most of all I love Those happy ones to whom 'tis life to live In single fervid faith and love unseeing, Drinking the blessed Amrit of my Being!
Now the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing, that ye may abound in hope, through the power of the Holy Ghost.
So wait patiently (O Muhammad) for thy Lord's decree, for surely thou art in Our sight; and hymn the praise of thy Lord when thou uprisest

source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text.en: You yourself must make an effort. The Tathagatas (Buddhas) are only preachers. The thoughtful who enter the way are freed from the bondage of Mara.

source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

text.en: Fearless is the Formless One, whose name is true, And whose creation is the whole world.

source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text.en: He is within all beings--and without-- Motionless, yet still moving; not discerned For subtlety of instant presence; close To all, to each; yet measurelessly far!
Beareth all things, believeth all things, hopeth all things, endureth all things.
Which is it, of the favours of your Lord, that ye deny ?

source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text.en: Cut out the love of self, like an autumn lotus, with thy hand! Cherish the road of peace. Nirvana has been shown by Sugata (Buddha).

source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

text.en: Pleasant is the night for those who long for Him in their hearts.

source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text.en: Wisdom He is And Wisdom's way, and Guide of all the wise, Planted in every heart.
And now abideth faith, hope, charity, these three; but the greatest of these is charity.
He is the First and the Last, and the Outward and the Inward; and He is Knower of all things.

source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text.en: The disciples of Gotama are always well awake, and their mind day and night always delights in compassion.

source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

ref: Asa ki War, Pauri VII (Guru Nanak)

text.en: Thou art the great Bestower; ever Thou givest gifts which increase a quarterfold.

source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text.en: Yet farther will I open unto thee This wisdom of all wisdoms, uttermost, The which possessing, all My saints have passed To perfectness.
Let all your things be done with charity.

He is Allah, than Whom there is no other God, the Sovereign Lord, the Holy One, Peace, the Keeper of Faith, the Guardian, the Majestic, the Compeller, the Superb. Glorified be Allah from all that they ascribe as partner (unto Him).

source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text.en: Good people shine from afar, like the snowy mountains; bad people are not seen, like arrows shot by night.

source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

text.en: He who meeteth the true Guru and fixeth God's name in his heart, obtaineth comfort.

source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text.en: And such-- With single, fervent faith adoring Me, Passing beyond the Qualities, conforms To Brahma, and attains Me!
But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith, Meekness, temperance: against such there is no law.
No calamity befalleth save by Allah's leave. And whosoever believeth in Allah, He guideth his heart. And Allah is Knower of all things.

source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text.en: An evil deed is better left undone, for a man repents of it afterwards; a good deed is better done, for having done it, one does not repent.

source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

ref: Asa ki War, Pauri X (Guru Nanak)

text.en: Be mine the gift of the dust of the saints' feet: if I obtain it, I shall apply it to my forehead.

source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text.en: For I am That whereof Brahma is the likeness! Mine The Amrit is; and Immortality Is mine; and mine perfect Felicity!
And above all these things put on charity, which is the bond of perfectness.

Let him who hath abundance spend of his abundance, and he whose provision is measured, let him spend of that which Allah hath given him. Allah asketh naught of any soul save that which He hath given it. Allah will vouchsafe, after hardship, ease.

source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text.en: They who know what is forbidden as forbidden, and what is not forbidden as not forbidden, such men, embracing the true doctrine, enter the good path.

source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

ref: Asa ki War, Slok XII (Guru Nanak)

text.en: Thou art the true Lord; beautiful is Thy praise; he who uttereth it is saved.

source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text.en: Are green and waving hymns which whisper Truth!
Be careful for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God.
And feed with food the needy wretch, the orphan and the prisoner, for love of Him, (Saying): We feed you, for the sake of Allah only. We wish for no reward nor thanks from you

source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text.en: Mules are good, if tamed, and noble Sindhu horses, and elephants with large tusks; but he who tames himself is better still.

source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

ref: Life of Guru Nanak (boyhood hymn to his schoolmaster)

text.en: Make divine love thy pen, and thy heart the writer; ask thy guru and write his instruction.

source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text.en: Know, too, from Me Shineth the gathered glory of the suns Which lighten all the world: from Me the moons Draw silvery beams, and fire fierce loveliness.
And the peace of God, which passeth all understanding, shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus.
He is successful who groweth, And remembereth the name of his Lord, so prayeth

source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text.en: This mind of mine went formerly wandering about as it liked, as it listed, as it pleased; but I shall now hold it in thoroughly, as the rider who holds the hook holds in the furious elephant.

source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

ref: Life of Guru Nanak (boyhood hymn to his schoolmaster)

text.en: Write God's name, write His praises, write that He hath neither end nor limit.

source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text.en: Now is the sacred, secret Mystery Declared to thee! Who comprehendeth this Hath wisdom! He is quit of works in bliss!
But my God shall supply all your need according to his riches in glory by Christ Jesus.
But ah! thou soul at peace! Return unto thy Lord, content in His good pleasure!

source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text.en: Pleasant is virtue lasting to old age, pleasant is a faith firmly rooted; pleasant is attainment of intelligence, pleasant is avoiding of sins.

source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

ref: Life of Guru Nanak (hymn to his mother)

text.en: O man, obey God and thou shalt be happy.

source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text.en: Be thou joyous, Prince! Whose lot is set apart for heavenly Birth.
Rejoice evermore. Pray without ceasing. In every thing give thanks: for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus concerning you.
He is indeed successful who causeth it to grow

source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text.en: The fields are damaged by weeds, mankind is damaged by hatred: therefore a gift bestowed on those who do not hate brings great reward.

source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

ref: Life of Guru Nanak (hymn to his mother)

text.en: Hail, hail to him who showeth the road! Hail, hail to him who communicateth the Word! Hail, hail to him who blendeth us with God!

source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text.en: Serenity of soul, benignity, Sway of the silent Spirit, constant stress To sanctify the Nature,--these things make Good rite, and true religiousness of Mind.
For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.
Thy Lord hath not forsaken thee nor doth He hate thee, And verily the latter portion will be better for thee than the former, And verily thy Lord will give unto thee so that thou wilt be content.

source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text.en: The Bhikshu who acts with kindness, who is calm in the doctrine of Buddha, will reach the quiet place (Nirvana), cessation of natural desires, and happiness.

source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

ref: Life of Guru Nanak (the husbandman hymn)

text.en: Become a husbandman, make good works thy soil, and the word of God thy seed; ever irrigate with the water of truth.

source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text.en: The gift lovingly given, when one shall say 'Now must I gladly give!'
Now faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen.
Therefor of the bounty of thy Lord be thy discourse.

source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text.en: Without knowledge there is no meditation, without meditation there is no knowledge: he who has knowledge and meditation is near unto Nirvana.

source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

ref: Life of Guru Nanak (Rag Asa verses)

text.en: He continueth to give us our daily bread which never faileth.

source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

So when thou art relieved, still toil And strive to please thy Lord.

source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text.en: Rouse thyself by thyself, examine thyself by thyself, thus self-protected and attentive wilt thou live happily, O Bhikshu!

source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

ref: Life of Guru Nanak (Rag Asa verses)

text.en: His praise is—that there neither is, Nor was, nor shall be any one like unto Him.

source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text.en: And whatsoever deeds he doeth--fixed In Me, as in his refuge--he hath won For ever and for ever by My grace Th' Eternal Rest!
Casting all your care upon him; for he careth for you.
Read: And thy Lord is the Most Bounteous

source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text.en: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who does not offend by body, word, or thought, and is controlled on these three points.

source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

ref: Life of Guru Nanak (hymn after the three days)

text.en: Wherever I look, there art Thou; if I am separated from Thee, I shall burst.

source: Max Arthur Macauliffe, The Sikh Religion (1909), Vol. I

text.en: So shalt thou come to Me! I promise true, For thou art sweet to Me!

text.ar: قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ (١) اللَّهُ الصَّمَدُ (٢)

source: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930)

text.en: Him I call indeed a Brahmana who utters true speech, instructive and free from harshness, so that he offend no one.

source: F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East Vol. X (1881)

text.en: (rendering: Reading book after book, the world has perished; none became truly learned. Whoever reads the two-and-a-half letters of love is the truly learned one.)

text.hi: बड़ा हुआ तो क्या हुआ, जैसे पेड़ खजूर। पंथी को छाया नहीं, फल लागे अति दूर॥
ऐसी बानी बोलिये, मन का आपा खोय। औरन को सीतल करे, आपहु सीतल होय॥
text.en: (rendering: Speak words that dissolve the ego of the mind; they cool others, and cool you too.)

text.hi: कबीरा खड़ा बाज़ार में, मांगे सबकी खैर। ना काहू से दोस्ती, ना काहू से बैर॥
text.en: (rendering: Kabir stands in the marketplace wishing well to all — friendship with none, enmity with none.)

text.hi: काल करे सो आज कर, आज करे सो अब। पल में परलय होयगी, बहुरि करेगा कब॥
text.en: (rendering: Do tomorrow’s work today, and today’s work now; in a moment comes dissolution — when will you do it then?)

text.hi: माया मरी न मन मरा, मर मर गए शरीर। आसा त्रिसना न मरी, कह गए दास कबीर॥
गुरु गोबिंद दोऊ खड़े, काके लागूँ पाँय। बलिहारी गुरु आपने, गोबिंद दियो बताय॥
text.en: (rendering: Guru and God both stand before me — whose feet shall I touch? Glory to the Guru, who showed me God.)

text.hi: दुख में सुमिरन सब करे, सुख में करे न कोय। जो सुख में सुमिरन करे, दुख काहे को होय॥
text.en: (rendering: All remember God in sorrow, none in joy. If one remembered Him in joy, why would sorrow come?)

text.hi: साईं इतना दीजिये, जामे कुटुंब समाय। मैं भी भूखा न रहूँ, साधु न भूखा जाय॥
निंदक नियरे राखिये, आँगन कुटी छवाय। बिन पानी साबुन बिना, निर्मल करे सुभाय॥
कस्तूरी कुंडलि बसै, मृग ढूँढै बन माहिं। ऐसे घटि घटि राम हैं, दुनिया देखै नाहिं॥
माला फेरत जुग भया, फिरा न मन का फेर। कर का मनका डारि दे, मन का मनका फेर॥
text.en: (rendering: Ages passed turning the rosary, yet the turning of the mind never ceased. Drop the beads of the hand; turn the beads of the mind.)

text.hi: जहाँ दया तहाँ धर्म है, जहाँ लोभ तहाँ पाप। जहाँ क्रोध तहाँ काल है, जहाँ छिमा तहाँ आप॥
तिनका कबहुँ न निंदिये, जो पाँयन तर होय। कबहुँ उड़ि आँखिन पड़े, पीर घनेरी होय॥
साधु ऐसा चाहिए, जैसा सूप सुभाय। सार सार को गहि रहे, थोथा देइ उड़ाय॥
हाड़ जले ज्यों लाकड़ी, केस जले ज्यों घास। सब जग जलता देखि कै, भया कबीर उदास॥
मंगल भवन अमंगल हारी। द्रवहु सुदसरथ अजिर बिहारी॥
सिया राम मय सब जग जानी। करउँ प्रनाम जोरि जुग पानी॥
राम नाम मनि दीप धरु, जीह देहरी द्वार। तुलसी भीतर बाहेरहुँ, जौ चाहसि उजियार॥
परहित सरिस धर्म नहिं भाई। परपीड़ा सम नहिं अधमाई॥
text.en: (rendering: Brother, there is no duty like doing good to others, and no baseness like causing others pain.)

text.hi: काम क्रोध मद लोभ की, जौ लौं मन में खान। तौ लौं पण्डित मूरखहुँ, तुलसी एक समान॥
तुलसी साथी बिपति के, बिद्या बिनय बिबेक। साहस सुकृत सुसत्य ब्रत, राम भरोसे एक॥
जहाँ सुमति तहँ संपति नाना। जहाँ कुमति तहँ बिपति निदाना॥
सकल पदारथ एहि जग माहीं। करमहीन नर पावत नाहीं॥
बुद्धिहीन तनु जानिके, सुमिरौं पवन कुमार। बल बुद्धि विद्या देहु मोहिं, हरहु कलेस विकार॥
जय हनुमान ज्ञान गुन सागर। जय कपीस तिहुँ लोक उजागर॥
text.en: (rendering: Victory to Hanuman, ocean of wisdom and virtue! Victory to the lord of monkeys, famed in all three worlds.)

text.hi: संकट कटै मिटै सब पीरा। जो सुमिरै हनुमत बलबीरा॥
राम दुआरे तुम रखवारे। होत न आज्ञा बिनु पैसारे॥
प्रबिसि नगर कीजै सब काजा। हृदय राखि कौसलपुर राजा॥
रहिमन धागा प्रेम का, मत तोड़ो चटकाय। टूटे से फिर न मिले, मिले गाँठ परि जाय॥
text.en: (rendering: Rahim says — do not snap the thread of love with a jerk; once broken it cannot be rejoined, and if joined, a knot remains.)

text.hi: रहिमन पानी राखिये, बिन पानी सब सून। पानी गए न ऊबरे, मोती मानुष चून॥
text.en: (rendering: Rahim says — guard your honour; without it all is barren. Once lost, neither pearl, man, nor lime can be revived.)

text.hi: जो रहीम उत्तम प्रकृति, का करि सकत कुसंग। चंदन विष व्यापत नहीं, लपटे रहत भुजंग॥
खीरा सिर तें काटिये, मलियत नमक लगाय। रहिमन कड़वे मुखन को, चहियत इहै सजाय॥
रहिमन देखि बड़ेन को, लघु न दीजिये डारि। जहाँ काम आवे सुई, कहा करे तरवारि॥
text.en: (rendering: Rahim says — seeing the great, do not discard the small; where a needle serves, what can a sword do?)

text.hi: तरुवर फल नहिं खात है, सरवर पियत न पान। कहि रहीम परकाज हित, संपति संचहिं सुजान॥
बिगरी बात बने नहीं, लाख करौ किन कोय। रहिमन फाटे दूध को, मथे न माखन होय॥
रहिमन निज मन की बिथा, मन ही राखो गोय। सुनि अठिलैहैं लोग सब, बाँटि न लैहै कोय॥

न जायते म्रियते वा कदाचिन्नायं भूत्वा भविता वा न भूयः। अजो नित्यः शाश्वतोऽयं पुराणो न हन्यते हन्यमाने शरीरे॥

(अर्थ: आत्मा न कभी जन्म लेती है, न कभी मरती है। वह अजन्मा, नित्य और सनातन है; शरीर के नष्ट होने पर भी वह नष्ट नहीं होती।)

यदा यदा हि धर्मस्य ग्लानिर्भवति भारत। अभ्युत्थानमधर्मस्य तदात्मानं सृजाम्यहम्॥

(अर्थ: हे भारत, जब-जब धर्म की हानि होती है और अधर्म बढ़ता है, तब-तब मैं स्वयं को प्रकट करता हूँ।)

सर्वधर्मान्परित्यज्य मामेकं शरणं व्रज। अहं त्वा सर्वपापेभ्यो मोक्षयिष्यामि मा शुचः॥

(अर्थ: समस्त धर्मों का आश्रय छोड़कर केवल मेरी शरण में आओ। मैं तुम्हें समस्त पापों से मुक्त कर दूँगा; शोक मत करो।)

ईशावास्यमिदं सर्वं यत्किञ्च जगत्यां जगत्। तेन त्यक्तेन भुञ्जीथा मा गृधः कस्यस्विद्धनम्॥

(अर्थ: इस जगत में जो कुछ भी है, वह सब ईश्वर से व्याप्त है। त्याग की भावना से भोग करो; किसी के धन का लोभ मत करो।)

सत्यमेव जयते नानृतं सत्येन पन्था विततो देवयानः॥

(अर्थ: सत्य की ही विजय होती है, असत्य की नहीं। सत्य के मार्ग से ही मोक्ष का मार्ग प्रशस्त होता है।)

उत्तिष्ठत जाग्रत प्राप्य वरान्निबोधत। क्षुरस्य धारा निशिता दुरत्यया दुर्गं पथस्तत्कवयो वदन्ति॥

(अर्थ: उठो, जागो और श्रेष्ठ ज्ञानियों से ज्ञान प्राप्त करो। ज्ञानीजन कहते हैं कि यह मार्ग छुरे की तीक्ष्ण धार के समान कठिन है।)

ॐ भूर्भुवः स्वः तत्सवितुर्वरेण्यं भर्गो देवस्य धीमहि धियो यो नः प्रचोदयात्॥

(अर्थ: हम उस पूजनीय सविता के श्रेष्ठ तेज का ध्यान करते हैं, जो हमारी बुद्धि को सन्मार्ग पर प्रेरित करे।)

text.sa: ॐ भूर्भुवः स्वः । तत्सवितुर्वरेण्यं भर्गो देवस्य धीमहि । धियो यो नः प्रचोदयात् ॥
text.en: (rendering: We meditate on the divine radiance of Savitar; may it inspire our minds.)

text.sa: असतो मा सद्गमय । तमसो मा ज्योतिर्गमय । मृत्योर्मा अमृतं गमय ॥
text.en: (rendering: Lead me from the unreal to the real, from darkness to light, from death to immortality.)
(rendering: Thou art That.)
(rendering: I am Brahman.)
(rendering: The whole world is one family.)
(rendering: Truth alone triumphs.)

text.sa: ईशावास्यमिदं सर्वं यत्किञ्च जगत्यां जगत् । तेन त्यक्तेन भुञ्जीथा मा गृधः कस्यस्विद्धनम् ॥
text.en: (rendering: All this, whatever moves in the world, is pervaded by the Lord. Enjoy through renunciation; covet no one’s wealth.)
(rendering: Arise, awake, and learn by approaching the wise.)
(rendering: The mind alone is the cause of man’s bondage and liberation.)
(rendering: May all beings everywhere be happy and free.)

text.sa: न जायते म्रियते वा कदाचिन्नायं भूत्वा भविता वा न भूयः । अजो नित्यः शाश्वतोऽयं पुराणो न हन्यते हन्यमाने शरीरे ॥
text.en: (rendering: Never is the Self born, nor does it die; unborn, eternal — it is not slain when the body is slain.)

text.sa: सर्वधर्मान्परित्यज्य मामेकं शरणं व्रज । अहं त्वां सर्वपापेभ्यो मोक्षयिष्यामि मा शुचः ॥
text.en: (rendering: Abandon all duties and take refuge in Me alone; I shall free you from all sins — grieve not.)

text.ar: بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ (١) الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ (٢) الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ (٣) مَالِكِ يَوْمِ الدِّينِ (٤) إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ وَإِيَّاكَ نَسْتَعِينُ (٥) اهْدِنَا الصِّرَاطَ الْمُسْتَقِيمَ (٦) صِرَاطَ الَّذِينَ أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ غَيْرِ الْمَغْضُوبِ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا الضَّالِّينَ (٧)
text.en: (rendering: The Opening — in the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful; praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds; guide us along the straight path.)

text.ar: إِنَّا أَعْطَيْنَاكَ الْكَوْثَرَ (١) فَصَلِّ لِرَبِّكَ وَانْحَرْ (٢) إِنَّ شَانِئَكَ هُوَ الْأَبْتَرُ (٣)
text.en: (rendering: We have granted you al-Kawthar; so pray to your Lord and sacrifice — your enemy is the one cut off.)

text.ar: وَالْعَصْرِ (١) إِنَّ الْإِنْسَانَ لَفِي خُسْرٍ (٢) إِلَّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ وَتَوَاصَوْا بِالْحَقِّ وَتَوَاصَوْا بِالصَّبْرِ (٣)
text.en: (rendering: By time — man is in loss, except those who believe, do good, and urge one another to truth and patience.)

text.ar: قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ الْفَلَقِ (١) مِنْ شَرِّ مَا خَلَقَ (٢) وَمِنْ شَرِّ غَاسِقٍ إِذَا وَقَبَ (٣) وَمِنْ شَرِّ النَّفَّاثَاتِ فِي الْعُقَدِ (٤) وَمِنْ شَرِّ حَاسِدٍ إِذَا حَسَدَ (٥)
text.en: (rendering: Say: I seek refuge with the Lord of the dawn, from the evil of what He created, and from the evil of the envier when he envies.)

text.ar: قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ النَّاسِ (١) مَلِكِ النَّاسِ (٢) إِلَهِ النَّاسِ (٣) مِنْ شَرِّ الْوَسْوَاسِ الْخَنَّاسِ (٤) الَّذِي يُوَسْوِسُ فِي صُدُورِ النَّاسِ (٥) مِنَ الْجِنَّةِ وَالنَّاسِ (٦)
text.en: (rendering: Say: I seek refuge with the Lord of mankind, the King of mankind, the God of mankind, from the evil of the retreating whisperer.)

text.pa: ਆਦਿ ਗੁਰਏ ਨਮਹ ॥ ਜੁਗਾਦਿ ਗੁਰਏ ਨਮਹ ॥ ਸਤਿਗੁਰਏ ਨਮਹ ॥ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਗੁਰਦੇਵਏ ਨਮਹ ॥
text.en: (rendering: I bow to the primal Guru, to the Guru of the ages, to the true Guru, to the great divine Guru.)

text.pa: ਸੋਚੈ ਸੋਚਿ ਨ ਹੋਵਈ ਜੇ ਸੋਚੀ ਲਖ ਵਾਰ ॥ ਚੁਪੈ ਚੁਪ ਨ ਹੋਵਈ ਜੇ ਲਾਇ ਰਹਾ ਲਿਵ ਤਾਰ ॥
text.en: (rendering: By thinking, He cannot be reduced to thought, though one think a hundred thousand times; by remaining silent, inner silence is not attained.)

text.pa: ਨਾਨਕ ਨਾਮ ਚੜ੍ਹਦੀ ਕਲਾ ॥ ਤੇਰੇ ਭਾਣੇ ਸਰਬੱਤ ਦਾ ਭਲਾ ॥
text.en: (rendering: Nanak: may the Name be ever ascendant; in Thy will, may all prosper.)
(rendering: Sukhmani — the jewel of peace; the ambrosial Name of the Lord.)

text.pa: ਵਾਹਿਗੁਰੂ ਜੀ ਕਾ ਖਾਲਸਾ ॥ ਵਾਹਿਗੁਰੂ ਜੀ ਕੀ ਫਤਹਿ ॥
text.en: (rendering: The Khalsa belongs to God; victory belongs to God.)
(rendering: True is the Name; wondrous is the Guru.)

text.pi: Manopubbaṅgamā dhammā, manoseṭṭhā manomayā; manasā ce paduṭṭhena, bhāsati vā karoti vā, tato naṃ dukkhamanveti, cakkaṃva vahato padaṃ.
text.en: (rendering: Mind precedes all things. If one speaks or acts with a corrupt mind, suffering follows as the wheel follows the foot of the ox.)

text.pi: Manopubbaṅgamā dhammā, manoseṭṭhā manomayā; manasā ce pasannena, bhāsati vā karoti vā, tato naṃ sukhamanveti, chāyāva anapāyinī.
text.en: (rendering: Mind precedes all things. If one speaks or acts with a pure mind, happiness follows like a shadow that never leaves.)
